title: DIREC: Diffusion-Based Review-Embedding Generation for Accurate Cross-Domain Recommendation

problem.claim: Cross-domain recommender systems aim to recommend target-domain items for users without target-domain interactions by using source-domain histories.

gap.claim: Embedding-transfer approaches may overlook fine-grained user-item preference signals expressed in reviews.

contributions.claim: A conditional-diffusion-based cross-domain recommender generates a target-domain review embedding and predicts the corresponding rating from it.
The method uses target-aware source attention to construct review guidance as a conditioning embedding.
The method pretrains on target-domain review embeddings from target-only users to learn a broader target-domain review-embedding distribution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three cross-domain scenarios reportedly show consistent improvement over nine competitors.
The reported maximum MAE reduction is 14.2%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain recommendation addresses target-domain recommendation without target-domain interactions.
Existing embedding-transfer approaches can miss fine-grained review-based preference signals.
The proposed conditional diffusion approach generates target-domain review embeddings for rating prediction, using target-aware attention and target-domain pretraining.
The authors report improvements across three cross-domain scenarios, including a maximum MAE reduction of 14.2%.

source_observation.claim: Fine-grained review signals may be missed when cross-domain recommendation relies mainly on transferred user embeddings.

interpretation.claim: Representing user-item-specific textual preference signals can complement domain-level user embedding transfer.

application.claim: For cross-domain recommendation, consider generating or modeling target-domain preference representations conditioned on source-domain history and target-item context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether generated review embeddings improve performance outside the reported scenarios or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, domain pairs, baselines, or statistical variability.
The abstract does not describe the diffusion architecture, training procedure, or ablation results.
